# D1. Main Depedent and Indepedent Variables (all models)

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(haven)
library(purrr)
library(kableExtra)

df <- readRDS("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UniversityofGlasgow/BES/BES/BES_subset_panel_full_v5_England.rds")
```

```{r helpers, include=FALSE}
# ── Generic helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
get_wave_num <- function(x) as.integer(str_extract(x, "\\d+$"))

waves_available <- function(df, base) {
  vars <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), paste0("^", base, "W\\d+$"))]
  sort(unique(map_int(vars, get_wave_num)))
}

# Pivot a single variable to long, returning id / wave / value
pivot_var <- function(df, base) {
  waves <- waves_available(df, base)
  cols  <- paste0(base, "W", waves)
  df |>
    select(id, all_of(cols)) |>
    mutate(across(all_of(cols), ~ as.numeric(zap_labels(.x)))) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = all_of(cols),
      names_to  = "wave",
      values_to = "value",
      names_pattern = paste0(base, "W(\\d+)$")
    ) |>
    mutate(wave = as.integer(wave)) |>
    filter(!is.na(value))
}

# Summarise a long variable tibble into one descriptive row
desc_row <- function(long_df, label, valid_range = NULL) {
  x <- long_df$value
  if (!is.null(valid_range)) x <- x[x >= valid_range[1] & x <= valid_range[2]]
  tibble(
    Variable     = label,
    Mean         = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD           = sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE),
    Min          = min(x,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Max          = max(x,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Observations = length(x),
    Respondents  = n_distinct(long_df$id[
      if (!is.null(valid_range))
        long_df$value >= valid_range[1] & long_df$value <= valid_range[2]
      else
        rep(TRUE, nrow(long_df))
    ])
  )
}
```

```{r main-vars-table}
# ── Variable definitions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
vars <- list(
  list(base = "immigSelf",     label = "Immigration self-placement (1–10)", range = c(0, 10)),
  list(base = "immigEcon",     label = "Immigration: economic impact (1–7)",  range = c(1, 7)),
  list(base = "immigCultural", label = "Immigration: cultural impact (1–7)",  range = c(1, 7)),
  list(base = "britishness",   label = "Britishness (1–7)",                   range = c(1, 7)),
  list(base = "englishness",   label = "Englishness (1–7)",                   range = c(1, 7))
)

desc_tbl <- map_dfr(vars, function(v) {
  long <- pivot_var(df, v$base)
  desc_row(long, v$label, valid_range = v$range)
})

desc_tbl |>
  mutate(
    Mean         = round(Mean, 3),
    SD           = round(SD,   3),
    Min          = round(Min,  0),
    Max          = round(Max,  0),
    Observations = formatC(Observations, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
    Respondents  = formatC(Respondents,  format = "d", big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  kbl(
    caption = "Table D1. Descriptive Statistics: Main Dependent and Independent Variables",
    align   = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    booktabs = TRUE
  ) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left") |>
  pack_rows("Dependent Variables", 1, 3) |>
  pack_rows("National Identity (Key Predictors)", 4, 5) |>
  footnote(
    general = paste(
      "Statistics computed over all valid person-wave observations.",
      "immigSelf is coded so that higher values indicate more permissive immigration attitudes.",
      "immigEcon and immigCultural are 7-point items coded so that higher values indicate",
      "more positive evaluations of immigration's economic and cultural impact respectively.",
      "Britishness and Englishness are 7-point items where higher values indicate",
      "stronger national identification."
    ),
    general_title = "Notes:",
    footnote_as_chunk = TRUE
  )
```

```{r plot-helpers, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# ── Shared theme ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_bjps <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      axis.title         = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text          = element_text(size = 9),
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0),
      plot.caption       = element_text(size = 8,  colour = "grey50", hjust = 0),
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.title       = element_blank()
    )
}

# Colour palette (colourblind-safe, 5 variables)
VAR_COLOURS <- c(
  "Immigration self-placement" = "#2166ac",
  "Econ. immigration attitudes" = "#4dac26",
  "Cultural immigration attitudes" = "#d01c8b",
  "Britishness"  = "#b35806",
  "Englishness"  = "#542788"
)

# ── Build long data for all five variables, with year ─────────────────────────
build_plot_long <- function(df) {
  
  var_specs <- list(
    list(base = "immigSelf",     label = "Immigration self-placement",     range = c(0, 10)),
    list(base = "immigEcon",     label = "Econ. immigration attitudes",     range = c(1, 7)),
    list(base = "immigCultural", label = "Cultural immigration attitudes", range = c(1, 7)),
    list(base = "britishness",   label = "Britishness",                    range = c(1, 7)),
    list(base = "englishness",   label = "Englishness",                    range = c(1, 7))
  )
  
  map_dfr(var_specs, function(v) {
    waves <- waves_available(df, v$base)
    cols  <- paste0(v$base, "W", waves)
    time_cols <- paste0("starttimeW", waves)
    
    # keep only time cols that exist
    time_cols_exist <- time_cols[time_cols %in% names(df)]
    waves_with_time <- as.integer(str_extract(time_cols_exist, "\\d+$"))
    
    df |>
      select(id,
             all_of(paste0(v$base, "W", waves_with_time)),
             all_of(paste0("starttimeW", waves_with_time))) |>
      mutate(across(
        all_of(paste0(v$base, "W", waves_with_time)),
        ~ as.numeric(zap_labels(.x))
      )) |>
      pivot_longer(
        cols         = -id,
        names_to     = c(".value", "wave"),
        names_pattern = "(.+)W(\\d+)$"
      ) |>
      mutate(
        wave  = as.integer(wave),
        year  = year(coalesce(
          suppressWarnings(ymd_hms(as.character(starttime), quiet = TRUE)),
          suppressWarnings(ymd(as.character(starttime),     quiet = TRUE))
        )),
        value = as.numeric(.data[[v$base]])
      ) |>
      rename(value_raw = value) |>
      mutate(
        value = case_when(
          value_raw >= v$range[1] & value_raw <= v$range[2] ~ value_raw,
          TRUE ~ NA_real_
        ),
        variable = v$label,
        scale    = paste0(v$range[1], "–", v$range[2])
      ) |>
      filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(wave)) |>
      select(id, wave, year, variable, scale, value)
  })
}

plot_long <- build_plot_long(df)
```

```{r histograms, fig.cap="Figure D1. Distribution of main dependent and independent variables (pooled person-wave observations).", fig.height=7, fig.width=9}

# ── Panel labels with scale annotation ───────────────────────────────────────
plot_long <- plot_long |>
  mutate(
    var_label = case_when(
      variable == "Immigration self-placement"     ~ "Immigration\nself-placement (0–10)",
      variable == "Econ. immigration attitudes"     ~ "Economic immigration\nattitudes (1–7)",
      variable == "Cultural immigration attitudes" ~ "Cultural immigration\nattitudes (1–7)",
      variable == "Britishness"                    ~ "Britishness (1–7)",
      variable == "Englishness"                    ~ "Englishness (1–7)"
    ),
    # preserve panel order
    var_label = factor(var_label, levels = c(
      "Immigration\nself-placement (0–10)",
      "Economic immigration\nattitudes (1–7)",
      "Cultural immigration\nattitudes (1–7)",
      "Britishness (1–7)",
      "Englishness (1–7)"
    )),
    group = if_else(
      variable %in% c("Britishness", "Englishness"),
      "National Identity", "Immigration Attitudes"
    )
  )

ggplot(plot_long, aes(x = value, fill = variable, colour = variable)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    binwidth = 1,
    boundary = 0.5,
    alpha    = 0.75,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = plot_long |>
      group_by(var_label) |>
      summarise(m = mean(value), .groups = "drop"),
    aes(xintercept = m),
    colour    = "grey20",
    linetype  = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = VAR_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = VAR_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  facet_wrap(~ var_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x       = "Response value",
    y       = "Density",
    caption = "Dashed line indicates the sample mean. Pooled person-wave observations; valid responses only."
  ) +
  theme_bjps()
```

```{r wave-means, fig.cap="Figure D2. Wave-specific means of main variables over time. Points show the sample mean; ribbons show ±1 SD. Dashed vertical lines mark key economic events.", fig.height=7, fig.width=10}

# ── Wave-level means and SDs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
wave_means <- plot_long |>
  group_by(variable, var_label, wave, year) |>
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value),
    sd_val   = sd(value),
    n        = n(),
    se       = sd_val / sqrt(n),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(year))

# Key economic events to annotate (adjust years to match your wave calendar)
events <- tibble(
  year  = c(2016, 2020, 2021, 2022),
  label = c("Brexit\nreferendum", "COVID-19\nonset", "Post-pandemic\nrecovery", "Cost-of-living\ncrisis")
)

ggplot(wave_means,
       aes(x = year, y = mean_val,
           colour = variable, fill = variable)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = mean_val - sd_val,
        ymax = mean_val + sd_val),
    alpha     = 0.10,
    colour    = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, shape = 21,
             colour = "white", stroke = 1.2,
             aes(fill = variable)) +
  geom_vline(
    data        = events,
    aes(xintercept = year),
    colour      = "grey50",
    linetype    = "dashed",
    linewidth   = 0.4,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data        = events,
    aes(x = year, y = Inf, label = label),
    angle       = 90,
    vjust       = 1.3,
    hjust       = 1.1,
    size        = 2.8,
    colour      = "grey40",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = VAR_COLOURS) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = VAR_COLOURS) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks  = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 6)) +
  facet_wrap(~ var_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Mean (±1 SD)",
    caption = paste(
      "Points are wave-level means; shaded bands are ±1 SD.",
      "Dashed lines mark key economic and political events.",
      "Valid person-wave observations only."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bjps() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## D2. Micro-Level Economic Variables

```{r desc-micro}
# income is stored as continuous equivalised weekly HH income (GBP)
# riskUnemployment is 0-10 scale

micro_vars <- list(
  list(base  = "income",
       label = "Equivalised household income (GBP/week)",
       range = NULL),          # continuous, no discrete range filter
  list(base  = "riskUnemployment",
       label = "Perceived unemployment risk (0–10)",
       range = c(0, 10))
)

desc_micro <- map_dfr(micro_vars, function(v) {
  long <- pivot_var(df, v$base)
  desc_row(long, v$label, valid_range = v$range)
})

desc_micro |>
  mutate(
    Mean         = round(Mean, 2),
    SD           = round(SD,   2),
    Min          = round(Min,  2),
    Max          = round(Max,  2),
    Observations = formatC(Observations, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
    Respondents  = formatC(Respondents,  format = "d", big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  kbl(
    caption  = "Table D2. Descriptive Statistics: Micro-Level Economic Variables",
    align    = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    booktabs = TRUE
  ) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left") |>
  pack_rows("Individual Economic Conditions", 1, 2) |>
  footnote(
    general = paste(
      "Equivalised household income is a continuous measure constructed under the",
      "OECD-modified equivalence scale (child weight = 0.3) and expressed in GBP per week.",
      "Perceived unemployment risk is a self-reported 0–10 scale where higher values",
      "indicate greater perceived likelihood of job loss.",
      "Observations differ across variables due to wave-varying item availability."
    ),
    general_title     = "Notes:",
    footnote_as_chunk = TRUE
  )
```

```{r hist-micro, fig.cap="Figure D4. Distribution of micro-level economic variables (pooled person-wave observations).", fig.height=4, fig.width=9}

MICRO_COLOURS <- c(
  "Equivalised household income (GBP/week)" = "#1b7837",
  "Perceived unemployment risk (0–10)"      = "#762a83"
)

micro_long <- map_dfr(micro_vars, function(v) {
  long <- pivot_var(df, v$base)
  if (!is.null(v$range)) {
    long <- long |> filter(value >= v$range[1], value <= v$range[2])
  }
  long |> mutate(variable = v$label)
}) |>
  left_join(
    # attach year via starttime
    map_dfr(waves_available(df, "starttime"), function(w) {
      col <- paste0("starttimeW", w)
      if (!col %in% names(df)) return(NULL)
      df |>
        select(id, all_of(col)) |>
        mutate(
          wave = w,
          year = year(coalesce(
            suppressWarnings(ymd_hms(as.character(.data[[col]]), quiet = TRUE)),
            suppressWarnings(ymd(as.character(.data[[col]]),     quiet = TRUE))
          ))
        ) |>
        select(id, wave, year)
    }),
    by = c("id", "wave")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    var_label = case_when(
      variable == "Equivalised household income (GBP/week)" ~
        "Equivalised household\nincome (GBP/week)",
      variable == "Perceived unemployment risk (0–10)" ~
        "Perceived unemployment\nrisk (0–10)"
    ),
    var_label = factor(var_label, levels = c(
      "Equivalised household\nincome (GBP/week)",
      "Perceived unemployment\nrisk (0–10)"
    ))
  )

# binwidth differs: continuous income needs wider bins than 0-10 risk scale
bw_map <- c(
  "Equivalised household\nincome (GBP/week)" = 10,
  "Perceived unemployment\nrisk (0–10)"      = 1
)

ggplot(micro_long, aes(x = value, fill = variable, colour = variable)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density),
        binwidth = bw_map[as.character(var_label)]),
    alpha     = 0.75,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = micro_long |>
      group_by(var_label) |>
      summarise(m = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    aes(xintercept = m),
    colour    = "grey20",
    linetype  = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = MICRO_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = MICRO_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels  = scales::percent_format()) +
  facet_wrap(~ var_label, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x       = "Value",
    y       = "Density",
    caption = "Dashed line indicates the sample mean. Pooled person-wave observations; valid responses only."
  ) +
  theme_bjps()

## D3. Meso-Level Economic Variables (Local Authority)

```{r setup-meso, include=FALSE}
library(sf)
library(scales)

# ── Meso variable specs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
meso_vars <- list(
  list(base  = "unemployment_rate",
       label = "LA unemployment rate (%)",
       range = c(0, 30)),          # APS unemployment rate, plausible ceiling
  list(base  = "claimant_rate",
       label = "LA claimant rate (% aged 16–64)",
       range = c(0, 25)),          # claimant_rate_16_64 plausible ceiling
  list(base  = "earnings_median",
       label = "LA median weekly earnings (GBP)",
       range = NULL)               # continuous, no ceiling needed
)

MESO_COLOURS <- c(
  "LA unemployment rate (%)"            = "#d6604d",
  "LA claimant rate (% aged 16–64)"     = "#4393c3",
  "LA median weekly earnings (GBP)"     = "#4dac26"
)

# ── Helper: pivot one meso variable to LA × wave long ─────────────────────────
pivot_meso_var <- function(df, base, valid_range = NULL) {
  cols  <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), paste0("^", base, "W\\d+$"))]
  waves <- as.integer(str_extract(cols, "\\d+$"))

  out <- df |>
    select(id, oslaua = any_of(paste0("oslauaW", waves[1])),
           all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols         = all_of(cols),
      names_to     = "wave",
      values_to    = "value",
      names_pattern = paste0("^", base, "W(\\d+)$")
    ) |>
    mutate(wave = as.integer(wave),
           value = as.numeric(value))

  if (!is.null(valid_range)) {
    out <- out |>
      mutate(value = if_else(
        value >= valid_range[1] & value <= valid_range[2],
        value, NA_real_
      ))
  }
  out |> filter(!is.na(value))
}

# ── Helper: attach fieldwork year to long meso panel ─────────────────────────
attach_year_meso <- function(long_df, df) {
  time_df <- map_dfr(sort(unique(long_df$wave)), function(w) {
    col <- paste0("starttimeW", w)
    if (!col %in% names(df)) return(NULL)
    df |>
      select(id, all_of(col)) |>
      mutate(
        wave = w,
        year = year(coalesce(
          suppressWarnings(ymd_hms(as.character(.data[[col]]), quiet = TRUE)),
          suppressWarnings(ymd(as.character(.data[[col]]),     quiet = TRUE))
        ))
      ) |>
      select(id, wave, year)
  })
  long_df |> left_join(time_df, by = c("id", "wave"))
}

# ── Helper: attach LA code (oslaua) across waves ──────────────────────────────
attach_la_code <- function(long_df, df) {
  la_cols <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), "^oslauaW\\d+$")]
  la_long <- df |>
    select(id, all_of(la_cols)) |>
    mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols         = all_of(la_cols),
      names_to     = "wave",
      values_to    = "la_code",
      names_pattern = "^oslauaW(\\d+)$"
    ) |>
    mutate(wave    = as.integer(wave),
           la_code = as.character(la_code)) |>
    filter(!is.na(la_code), la_code != "")

  long_df |>
    mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
    left_join(la_long, by = c("id", "wave"))
}
```

```{r build-meso-long, include=FALSE}
# Build full long panel for all three meso variables
meso_long <- map_dfr(meso_vars, function(v) {
  pivot_meso_var(df, v$base, v$range) |>
    attach_year_meso(df) |>
    attach_la_code(df) |>
    mutate(variable = v$label)
}) |>
  mutate(
    var_label = factor(variable, levels = map_chr(meso_vars, "label"))
  )

# LA × year panel (deduplicated — one value per LA per year per variable)
la_year_panel <- meso_long |>
  filter(!is.na(la_code), !is.na(year)) |>
  group_by(variable, var_label, la_code, year) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

## D4. Macro-Level Economic Variables (England)

```{r setup-meso, include=FALSE}
#| label: setup-macro-desc
#| include: false

library(scales)

# ── Macro variable specs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
macro_vars <- list(
  list(
    base  = "unempl_rate",
    label = "National unemployment rate (%)",
    range = c(0, 30)
  ),
  list(
    base  = "claimant_k",
    label = "National claimant count (thousands)",
    range = NULL
  ),
  list(
    base  = "gdp_pc",
    label = "GDP per capita (GBP)",
    range = NULL
  ),
  list(
    base  = "cpih_rate",
    label = "CPIH inflation rate (%)",
    range = NULL
  )
)

MACRO_COLOURS <- c(
  "National unemployment rate (%)"       = "#d6604d",
  "National claimant count (thousands)"  = "#4393c3",
  "GDP per capita (GBP)"                 = "#4dac26",
  "CPIH inflation rate (%)"              = "#9970ab"
)

# ── Helper: pivot one macro variable to respondent × wave long ────────────────
pivot_macro_var <- function(df, base, valid_range = NULL) {

  cols <- names(df)[
    str_detect(names(df), paste0("^", base, "W\\d+$"))
  ]

  out <- df |>
    select(id, all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols          = all_of(cols),
      names_to      = "wave",
      values_to     = "value",
      names_pattern = paste0("^", base, "W(\\d+)$")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      wave  = as.integer(wave),
      value = as.numeric(value)
    )

  if (!is.null(valid_range)) {
    out <- out |>
      mutate(
        value = if_else(
          value >= valid_range[1] & value <= valid_range[2],
          value,
          NA_real_
        )
      )
  }

  out |>
    filter(!is.na(value))
}


# ── Helper: attach fieldwork year to long macro panel ─────────────────────────
attach_year_macro <- function(long_df, df) {

  time_df <- map_dfr(
    sort(unique(long_df$wave)),
    function(w) {

      col <- paste0("starttimeW", w)

      if (!col %in% names(df)) return(NULL)

      df |>
        select(id, all_of(col)) |>
        mutate(
          wave = w,
          year = year(
            coalesce(
              suppressWarnings(
                ymd_hms(as.character(.data[[col]]), quiet = TRUE)
              ),
              suppressWarnings(
                ymd(as.character(.data[[col]]), quiet = TRUE)
              )
            )
          )
        ) |>
        select(id, wave, year)
    }
  )

  long_df |>
    left_join(time_df, by = c("id", "wave"))
}

```

```{r build-macro-long, include=FALSE}
#| label: build-macro-long
#| include: false

# Build full long panel for all four macro variables
macro_long <- map_dfr(macro_vars, function(v) {

  pivot_macro_var(
    df,
    v$base,
    v$range
  ) |>
    attach_year_macro(df) |>
    mutate(variable = v$label)

}) |>
  mutate(
    var_label = factor(
      variable,
      levels = map_chr(macro_vars, "label")
    )
  )


# ── National × year panel ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Macro indicators are repeated across BES respondents.
# Collapse to one national value per year per variable.

national_year_panel <- macro_long |>
  filter(!is.na(year)) |>
  group_by(
    variable,
    var_label,
    year
  ) |>
  summarise(
    value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

      "CPIH: ONS Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs, all items (2015 = 100), aggregated to annual values from the quarterly observations reported in the ONS series.",
      "For each BES wave, annual macroeconomic values were assigned according to the median calendar year of wave fieldwork."
      
    ),
    
    general_title     = "Notes:",
    
    footnote_as_chunk = TRUE
    
  )
